newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold market depressed with onset of summer.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold market depressed with onset of summer.

text.p: The onset of the long hot Arabian summer and the exodus of expatriate workers for holidays has dragged down the Dubai gold market, traders said on Sunday.
Tourists are staying away due to the heat, and demand from the Indian subcontinent is weak as investors wait to see what riches the monsoon there will bring, they added.
"The market is subdued at the moment. The price of gold is bottoming out," said one trader.
"If the monsoon (in India) is good, which we will be able to tell by the end of June, purchasing power should be up and the gold market should improve, but at the moment demand is weak," he added.
India's June to September monsoon season is the prelude to the start of the country's main wedding season when imports from supply markets, particularly Dubai, increase.
"Indian demand has decreased because the monsoon is only really starting now," said a gold retailer.
Dubai traders said lower world bullion prices dragged down the price of Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar in the week.
They quoted the TT bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- at 4,672 dirhams ($1,273) on Sunday, down from 4,720 dirhams a week earlier.
During the week, spot gold on the international bullion market broke below $340 an ounce to end the week quoted at $337.40/90, the lowest weekly close since April 1993.
Gold was last quoted on Saturday at $337.75/338.25 an ounce, down from $341.10/60 last week.

Dubai traders said they had been disappointed by low sales at the start of the summer holiday season. Usually this is a good time for the market as expatriates, mainly from the Indian subcontinent, traditionally return home for the summer holidays with gifts of gold jewellery and investment bars.
But traders said some customers had taken advantage of a special gold promotion during the March-April Dubai shopping festival to stock up on summer gifts.
"People have already bought their gold presents during the festival," said one trader.
Local retail sales were also capped by expectations of further weakness in the gold price.
"Everyone thinks it will go down further, so they are waiting for the cheaper prices," a trader said, adding UAE buyers were particularly price sensitive.
